The following Ordinance made by the Governor of Sindh is hereby published for

3. Establishment of the
Institute.‑‑‑ (1) There shall be established an Institute
at Karachi with the status and functions of a Degree awarding Institute to be
known as the Khadim Ali Shah, Bukhari Institute of Technology consisting of‑‑‑
(i) the Patron,
the Chairman, the Director, the Dean and such other officers as may be
prescribed;
(ii) the members
of such councils, committees and other bodies as the Board may establish;
(iii) the
teachers and students of the Institute and its constituent units; and
(iv) such other
officers and members of the staff as may from time to time be specified by the
Board.
(2) The
Institute shall be a body corporate by the name of the Khadim Ali Shah Bukhari
Institute of Technology, owned, managed and administered by the Kasbit having
perpetual succession and a common seal with powers among others to acquire,
hold and dispose of movable and immovable properties and shall sue and be sued
by the said name.
(3) The
Institute shall have powers to set up any additional campus within the
jurisdiction of the Institute i.e. Karachi.

Powers and functions of the Institute

ORDINANCE XXII OF 2001
ORDINANCE XXII OF 2001
KHADIM ALI SHAH

ORDINANCE, .2001.
An Ordinance to
provide for the establishment of

[Gazette of Sindh,

28th June, 2001]
No. S.LEGIS.l(22)2001, dated 28‑6‑2001.‑‑‑
The following Ordinance made by the Governor of Sindh is hereby published for
general information:‑‑‑
4. Powers and functions of the
Institute.‑‑‑ Subject to the instructions prescribed by
Government or the University Grants Commission, the Institute shall have the
powers‑‑
(a) to provide
for instruction and training in economics management, basic applied and
computer sciences and technology, and other allied disciplines in such a manner
as it considers appropriate;
(b) to conduct
seminars, conferences, workshops and such other functions which are necessary
for curricular and extra‑curricular objectives o the Institute;
(c) to print,
publish and circulate periodicals journals; magazine; and books and disseminate scientific, technological and other
relate knowledge and information conducive to the attainment of any of the
objectives of the Institute;
(d) to promote
contact and establish linkage and affiliate with other universities, institutions
and development organizations of effective discharge of its functions and
responsibilities;
(e) to admit and
examine students and to confer or award degrees. diplomas, certificates and
other academic distinctions on and to the persons. who have passed its
examinations under the prescribed conditions;
(f) to confer
honorary decrees or other distinctions on approved persons in the prescribed
manner;
(g) to prescribe
courses of studies and undertake research as it may determine;
(h) to provide
for the teaching of specified courses and training for the persons not being
the students of the Institute and grant certificates and diplomas to such
persons;
(i) to receive
and manage properties, grants, bequests, trusts, gifts. donations, endowments
and other contributions made to the Institute and to invest them in such manner
as it may deem fit;
(j) to enter
into agreements, contracts and arrangements with any Government, organization,
institution, body or individual for carrying out its functions and activities;
(k) to demand
and receive such fees and other charges as it may determine; provided that ten
per cent. seats will be reserved for meritorious, poor candidates on free ship
or scholarship basis;
(1) to supervise
and control the discipline of the students of the institute as may be
prescribed;
(m) to appoint
,members of various bodies and committees, for instructional and curricular
activities and admit students of the Institute and its constituent units;
(n) to appoint
such officers including teachers and members of the non‑teaching staff
and prescribe terms and 'conditions, powers and duties of such officers and
staff; and
(o) to do all
such other acts and things as may be required to further its objectives.

5. Institute open to all.‑‑‑
The Institute shall be open to all persons of either sex and whatever religion,
race, creed, caste, colour or domicile who are academically qualified for
admission to the courses of study offered by the Institute and no such person
shall be denied the privilege on the ground only of sex, religion, race, class,
creed, caste, colour or domicile.

9. Visitation.‑‑‑
(1) The Patron may cause an inspection or inquiry to be made in respect of any
matter connected with the affairs of the Institute and shall, from time to
time, direct any person or persons to inquire into or carry out inspection of‑‑
.
(i) the
Institute, its buildings, laboratories, libraries, and other facilities;
(ii) any
institution, department or hostel maintained by the Institute;
(iii) the
adequacy of financial and human resources;
(iv) the
teaching, research, curriculum, examination and other matters of the Institute;
and
(v) such other
matters as may be specified by him.
(2) The patron
shall communicate to the Board his views with regard to the results of the
visitation and shall, after ascertaining the views of the Board, advise the
Board, on the actions to be taken by it.
(3) The Board
shall, within such time as may be specified by the Patron, communicate to him
such action, if any, as has been taken or may be proposed to be taken upon the
results of vitiation.
(4) Where the
Board does not, within the time specified, take action to the satisfaction of
the Patron, the Patron may issue such directions as he deems fit and the Board
shall comply with all such directions.
(5) The Patron shall have full powers to take any action as
he may deem fit against the institute, including its closure, if found
indulging in any subversive or unlawful activity. '

10. The Chairman.‑‑‑
(1) The Patron shall appoint the Chairman from a panel of three persons of
eminence known for the contribution in the field of knowledge or education
submitted by the Kasbit.
(2) The Chairman
shall in the absence of the Patron preside over the convocation.
(3) If the
Chairman is satisfied that the proceedings of any Authority or order of any
officer are not in accordance with the provisions of this Ordinance, he may,
after calling upon such Authority or officer to show cause why such proceedings
should not be annulled, by order in writing, annul such proceedings or orders.
(4) Should the
Chairman be incapacitated to act due to any cause, the Director shall act in
lieu thereof.

11. Director.‑‑‑
(1) The Director shall be appointed by the Chairman, on the recommendation of
the Board on such terms and conditions as the Board may determine.
(2) The Director
shall have the following powers:‑‑
(a) to approve
and sanction in contingencies expenses not provided for in the budget for an
amount not exceeding Rs.1 million per campus;
(b) to re
appropriate any amount provided for in the budget to another category within
the campus or inter campus;
(c) to approve
administrative operational and organizational procedures and ensure effective
implementation thereof;
(d) to appoint
individuals, committees or groups to carry out visitations, inquiries, studies
or investigation into any affairs of the Institute; and
(e), to exercise
and perform such other powers and functions as may be assigned by the Board.

The following Ordinance made by the Governor of Sindh is hereby published for

14. The Board.‑‑‑
(1) The general supervision and control of the affairs and the powers to lay
down the policies o he Institute h vest in the Board consisting of the
following member‑‑
(i) the
Chairman;
(ii) a Judge of
the High Court of Sindh nominated by the Chief Justice;
(iii) Director;
(iv) the
Secretary, Education Department, Government of Sindh or his nominee;
(v) the
Chairman, University Grants Commission or his nominee;
(vi) one member
of the Educational (non‑Government Organization) to be nominated by the
Kasbit;
(vii) three
persons of outstanding merit, to be nominated by the Kasbit; and
(viii) Chairman,
Chamber of Commerce and Industries Sindh or his nominee.
(2) The Director
shall also act as the Secretary.
(3) A nominated
member shall hold office for a term of three years, and shall be eligible for re nomination on the expiry of his term.
(4) The office
of a nominated member shall become vacant if he resigns or fails to attend
three consecutive meetings of the Board without sufficient cause or leave of
absence or the authority nominated him changes his nomination.
(5) The
authority, which had nominated the member whose vacancy is to be filled, shall
fill a casual vacancy of a member.
(6) No act or
proceedings of the Board shall be invalid by reasons only of the existence of a
vacancy in or a defect in the constitution of the Board.

sections.shortTitle: Khadim Ali Shah Bukhari Institute of Technology Ordinance 2001

Powers and Functions of the Board

ORDINANCE XXII OF 2001
ORDINANCE XXII OF 2001

No. S.LEGIS.l(22)2001, dated 28‑6‑2001.‑‑‑
The following Ordinance made by the Governor of Sindh is hereby published for
general information:‑‑‑
15. Powers and Functions of the Board.‑‑‑ The Board shall exercise and
perform the powers and functions as follows:‑‑
(i) to hold,
control of and administer the properties, funds, assets and resources of the
Institute;
(ii) to transfer
and accept transfer of movable or immovable property on behalf of the
Institute;
(iii) to
consider and approve the advice of the Finance and Planning Committee, the
annual and revised budget estimate and to lay down guidelines or rules of
business dealing with financial, academic and administrative matters of the
Institute;
(iv) to approve,
carry out, vary or cancel contracts on behalf of the Institute;
(v) to initiate
and approve schemes for achievement of the objectives of the Institute;
(vi) to
determine the form, and regulate the custody and use of common seal of the
Institute;
(vii) to create
professional, research, administrative posts and such other posts as may be
required to carry out the purposes of the Institute, and suspend or abolish
such posts;
(viii) to
appoint teachers, researchers, officers and the employees on the
recommendations of the Selection Board;
(ix) to suspend,
punish and remove from service the Institute teachers, researchers, officers
and employees whom it is empowered to appoint, in the manner prescribed after
due enquiry;
(x) to .propose
regulations for submission to the Chairman for approval;
(xi) to approve
rules on the recommendations of the appropriate bodies or authorities to
regulate any matter relating to the affairs of the Institute; and
(xii) to
determine, regulate and administer all other matters concerning the Institute
and, to this end, exercise all necessary powers not specifically mentioned in
the Ordinance or rules.
(2) The Board
may delegate any 6f its powers to any Authority or officer or a committee as it
deems fit.

The following Ordinance made by the Governor of Sindh is hereby published for
general information:‑‑‑
16. Meeting of the Board.‑‑‑
(1) The Board shall meet at least twice in a year provided that a, special
meeting may be called at any time on the direction of the Chairman or on a
requisition made by not less than four members of the Board to consider a
matter of urgent nature
(2) The meetings
shall be presided over by the Chairman and in his absence by the Director.
(3) Not less
than 7 clear days' notice of a special meeting shall be given to the members of
the Board and the agenda of the meeting shall be restricted to the matter for
,which the special meeting is called.
(4) The quorum for
a meeting of the Board shall be one‑half of its members, a fraction being
counted as one.
(5) The
decisions of the Board shall be expressed in terms of the views of the majority
of the members present and voting and, if the members are equally divided, the
Chairman shall have a casting vote.

17. Academic Council.‑‑‑
(1) The Academic Council shall consist of‑‑‑
(i) The Director,
who shall be the Chairman;
(ii) the Deans;
(iii) the
Chairmen of the Teaching Departments;
(iv) the
Professors of the Institute;
(v) nominee of
,.University Grants Commission or
Academic Advisor;
(vi) nominee of
the Education Secretary not below the rank of Deputy Secretary; and
(vii) five
eminent scholars to be nominated by the Board.
(2) The
nominated member shall hold office for a term of three years, and shall be
eligible for renomination.
(3) The office
of a nominated member shall become vacant if he resigns or fails to attend
three consecutive meetings of the Council without sufficient cause or leave of
absence or the nominating authority changes his nomination.
(4) The quorum
for a meeting of the Council shall be one‑half of the total number of
members, a fraction being counted as one.

ORDINANCE XXII OF 2001

28th June, 2001]
No. S.LEGIS.l(22)2001, dated 28‑6‑2001.‑‑‑
The following Ordinance made by the Governor of Sindh is hereby published for
general information:‑‑‑
18. Powers and functions of
the Academic Council.‑‑‑ (1) The Academic Council shall be
the highest academic body of the Institute, and shall, subject to the
provisions of this Ordinance and the regulations, have the powers to lay down
proper standards of instructions, research and examinations and to regulate and
promote the academic life of the Institute.
(2) In
particular and without prejudice to the generality of the foregoing provisions,
the Council shall have the powers‑‑
(i) to advise
the Board on academic matters;
(ii) to regulate
the admission of students to the courses of studies and examinations;
(iii) to propose
to the Board, schemes for the constitution and organization of faculties
teaching departments; campuses and Board of Studies;
(iv) to consider
or formulate proposals for the planning and development of teaching and research
in the Institute;
(v) to make
regulations, on the recommendations of the Board of Studies, prescribing the
course of studies and the syllabi for all Institute examinations:
Provided that,
if the recommendations of the Board of Studies are not received by the
prescribed date, the Council may, subject to the approval of the Board,
continue for the next year the courses of studies already prescribed for an
examination;
(vi) td
recognize the examinations of other Universities or examining bodies as equivalent
to the corresponding examinations of the Institute;
(vii) to frame
regulations for submission to the Board;
(viii) to
appoint members to the various authorities in accordance with the provisions of
this Ordinance; and
(ix) to perform
such other functions as may be prescribed.

No. S.LEGIS.l(22)2001, dated 28‑6‑2001.‑‑‑
The following Ordinance made by the Governor of Sindh is hereby published for
general information:‑‑‑
19. The Institute fund, audit
and accounts.‑‑‑ (1) The Institute shall have a fund to
which shall be credited income from fees, donations, trusts, bequests,
endowments, grants, contributions and all other sources.
(2) Capital and
recurrent expenditure of the Institute shall be met from the contributions made by any source including foundations,
universities and individuals, and from the income derived from such sources
provided that Institute may obtain funds from the Kasbit according to the terms
and conditions agreed upon.
(3) No
contribution, donation or grant which may directly of indirectly involve any
immediate or subsequent financial liability for the Institute or which may
involve an activity not included in the programmes shall be accepted without
the prior approval of the Board.
(4) The accounts
of the Institute shall be maintained in such form and manner as may be
determined by the Board and shall be audited each year within four months of
the closing of the financial year of the Institute by the Chartered Accountant
appointed by the Board.
(5) The accounts
together with the report of the auditor thereon, shall be submitted to the
Board for approval.
(6) The auditor
shall certify that the auditor has complied with the standards of audit and
certification laid down by the Institute of Chartered Accountants of Pakistan.

The following Ordinance made by the Governor of Sindh is hereby published for
general information:‑‑‑
22. Regulations.‑‑‑
(1) Subject to the provisions of this Ordinance, the Board may make regulations
which may prescribe all or any of the following matters namely‑‑‑
(a) terms and
conditions of service of employees of the Institute, including scales of pay,
constitution of pension, insurance, gratuity, provident fund, benevolent fund
and other fringe benefits;
(b) terms and
conditions of contractual appointment of teachers, researchers and other
officers and staff;
(c) constitution
and functions of the Selection Board for selection of candidates for
appointment to various posts of teachers, researchers and other officers and
staff;
(d)
establishment of faculties, teaching departments and other academic units and
divisions and their management;
(e) powers and
duties of officers and teachers;
(f)
arrangements, partnership, collaboration with other public, Government or
private organizations for purpose of instruction, research and other scholarly
activities for the betterment of the Institute;
(g) conditions
of appointment of Professor Emeritus and Distinguished Professors; '
(h) award of
honorary degrees;
(i) standards
for evaluation of efficiency and exercising disciplinary measures over the
employees of the Institute;
(j) acquisition
and administration of properties and investment of the Institute; and
(k) all other
matters which under this Ordinance are required to be or may be prescribed by
the regulations.
(2) The draft of
the regulations shall be proposed by the Board for approval by the Chairman who
may refer them back to the Board for reconsideration.
(3) The Chairman
shall have the powers to assent to the regulations submitted to him for
approval.
(4) No
regulation shall be valid until assented to and, signed by the Chairman. ,

25. Removal of difficulties.‑‑‑
(1) If any difficulty .arises in giving effect to any of the provisions of this
Ordinance, the Chairman may make such orders, which are consistent with the
provisions of this Ordinance. ‑
(2) Where this
Ordinance makes any provision for anything to be done, but no provision or
insufficient provision has been made as respecting the authority by whom, or
the time at which, or the manner in which it shall be done then it shall be
done by such authority, or at such time, or in such manner, as the Chairman may
direct.
